Jake — thanks for the clear summary and the form. I want to make sure we align with Acme’s signoff timeline — they’ve told Ben they’d like proofs before the order form is routed for signature.

Quick responses / asks from our side:
- Limits: Redwood’s standard is GL 1M each / 2M aggregate, E&O 1M, Cyber 1M (we can consider 2M for this deal if Acme insists; need approval from finance).
- Additional insured: we typically accept an additional insured endorsement on GL/Auto limited to liability caused by our services; we do not add AI model outputs as an explicit insured category.
- Waiver of subrogation: we prefer not to give a blanket waiver across all policies; acceptable on Auto/GL if carrier confirms and it doesn’t expand their exposure.
- Certificate holder address you have is correct.

Neha — can you confirm whether we should require the ISO CG 20 26 (or equivalent) endorsement language and whether the MSA redline should explicitly exclude professional liability from additional insured? If you prefer, I’ve attached our internal requirements (Redwood_insurance_requirements_v2.pdf) to guide the broker.

3) Ben: keep Acme procurement updated and flag if they will push back on limits (may require a small credit conversation).

Thanks all — aiming for COI + endorsement draft by EOD Aug 19 if possible.

Logan / team —

Reviewed the requirements and the suggested routing. My notes for the MSA/order form redline and what we should require from the broker:

1) Additional insured: require an endorsement limited to liability arising out of Redwood’s performance of services for Acme. Do NOT broaden to professional liability (E&O/PI) — additional insured on PI is not standard and carriers usually decline. I recommend language like: "Additional Insured — as respects liability arising out of the Named Insured’s operations or services performed for the Additional Insured under written contract."

2) ISO endorsements: ask for CG 20 26 and CG 20 10 samples (or insurer equivalent). If carrier provides a manuscript endorsement, request an insurer letter confirming that the endorsement provides materially equivalent coverage.

3) Waiver of subrogation: acceptable on GL and Auto if carrier confirms in writing; do not require on Professional Liability or Cyber unless the insurer voluntarily agrees.

4) Retroactive/prior acts date: for claims-made policies (PL/Cyber), request the retroactive date and that it precedes the effective date of the services/pilot. If the carrier cannot provide retroactive coverage, we’ll need to discuss risk acceptance.

5) Proof: COI alone is not sufficient for Acme’s legal— they generally want the endorsement attached and (for higher-risk deals) an insurer letter confirming limits/retroactive dates. Ask broker to deliver: COI, endorsement PDF, and insurer letter.

I’ve drafted a short snippet for the MSA redline paragraph on insurance which I can paste into the order form if helpful. Attaching the snippet now.

Neha Kapoor
